problem:
For the sets $Z={-3,6,-9}$ and $Y=Z\times Z,$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- $(-3,6,-3)\in Y$
- $(-3,-9)\in Y$
- $(-9,6)\in Y$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $Z\times Z$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $Z$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $Z.$

In this case, the schematic for ${Z}^{2}=Z\times Z$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/0c58bf1f025cc4960ce3b9dc8e1bc3bf474a521473833b27d136fd77fd6b814a.png)

Hence, the set $Y=Z\times Z$ is given by

$$
Y={(-3,-3),(-3,6),(-3,-9),(6,-3),(6,6),(6,-9),(-9,-3)(-9,6),(-9,-9)}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
